input: # What `compat: 'apidef'` gives where apidef's reading of a reference
# parts from the specification's. Each expected value is what
# @voxgig/apidef's own resolver gives for the row's input, at the
# row's select path: `node tools/apidef-preset.cjs <apidef checkout>
# --ref 3b24341 --sets rows --rows test/resolve/apidef-extra.tsv` holds
# every row to it. The unresolved and cuts columns are this resolver's
# report. A fixture compares without member order, and
# ts/test/resolve.test.ts pins that.
# Only a pointer written #/... names anything. The whole document, by # or by an empty reference, is left as written.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#"},"B":{"$ref":""},"C":{"type":"string"}}}}
# An anchor is not read, in 3.1 as before it.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"$anchor":"tee","type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"#tee"}}}}
# A reference by the document's own URI is not read: it has a document part.

{"openapi":"3.2.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"https://example.com/api#/components/schemas/T"}}},"$self":"https://example.com/api"}
# Nor is one by the URI of a schema that declares $id.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"$id":"https://example.com/t","type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"https://example.com/t"}}}}
# A pointer is read from the root of the document, whatever $id is in force where it is written.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$id":"https://example.com/a","$ref":"#/components/schemas/C"},"C":{"type":"string"}}}}
# So a pointer meant for the schema that declares $id finds nothing at the root.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"$id":"https://example.com/t","$defs":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/$defs/x"}}}}}}
# A pointer is not percent-decoded: the member named is the one written.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"a b":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/a%20b"},"B":{"$ref":"#%2Fcomponents%2Fschemas%2FC"},"C":{"type":"number"}}}}
# A member whose name has a percent sign is named as written.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"100%":{"type":"string"},"a%20b":{"type":"number"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/100%"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/a%20b"}}}}
# A tilde that begins no escape is itself, and ~1 and ~0 are the only escapes.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"a~":{"type":"string"},"b~2c":{"type":"number"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/a~"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/b~2c"}}}}
# A schema dialect is not read: a reference under one this package does not support still resolves.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"B":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#","properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"}}}}},"jsonSchemaDialect":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#"}
# $dynamicRef is not read at all.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"$dynamicAnchor":"d","type":"string"},"A":{"$dynamicRef":"#d","$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"B":{"$dynamicRef":"#d"}}}}
# A reference met on the way is followed before the next member is read. One that names nothing ends the walk, though the map as written has the member: here in another document, and missing.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"B":{"$ref":"./other.yaml#/B","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}},"C":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B/properties/x"},"M":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}},"D":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/M/properties/x"}}}}
# One that resolves is read through: its own members are found, and its target's.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"p":{"type":"string"}}},"M":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","properties":{"q":{"type":"number"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/M/properties/q"}}}}
# A $ref that is not a string makes no reference, so a pointer reads through its map.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":5,"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"}}},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/p"}}}}
# The root is where pointers start, and is never a site: its $ref stays, with no x-ref.
# A root that is a reference is followed before any pointer is read, and following it needs the root again: no pointer in the document names anything.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"}}}}
# A member named __proto__ beside a $ref is left out of a site that resolves, and stays in one that does not.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"string"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","__proto__":0},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope","__proto__":0}}}}
# A pointer that enters a cycle by one reference, and steps through the reference that closes it, lands.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A"}}},"E":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/p/properties/p"}}}}
# The same document: the reference that closes the cycle holds what it names, with its x-ref.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A"}}},"E":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/p/properties/p"}}}}
# A reference that closes a cycle resolves in place when a reference written before it names it.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C/properties/q"},"C":{"properties":{"q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C"}}}}}}
# The same document: the earlier reference holds the cycle too.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C/properties/q"},"C":{"properties":{"q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C"}}}}}}
# A container that a reference written before it names, and that holds a reference to its own parent, is resolved where it stands.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","info":{"title":"t","version":"1"},"paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"X":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/P/properties/t"},"P":{"properties":{"t":{"properties":{"up":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/P"}}}}}}}}
